record.context_brief: Problem 3: nonzero solutions to homogeneous equations
record.original_question: Given a homogeneous polynomial P(x1, ..., xn) with integer coefficients, determine whether the equation P(x1, ..., xn) = 0 has an integer solution in which every variable is nonzero.

evidence.quote: For homogeneous equations, this question reduces to the following problem.
Problem 3. Given a homogeneous polynomial P(x1, . . . , xn) with integer coefficients, determine whether equation (1) has an integer solution such that all variables are different from 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P(x_1, \dots, x_n) \in \mathbb{Z}[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ be a homogeneous polynomial with integer coefficients. Provide a general algorithm which, given $P$ as input, decides whether the equation
$$P(x_1, \dots, x_n) = 0$$
admits a solution $(x_1, \dots, x_n) \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ with $x_i \neq 0$ for every $i \in \{1, \dots, n\}$. Equivalently, determine whether the problem of detecting the existence of such an all-nonzero integer solution to an arbitrary homogeneous integer polynomial equation is decidable.
artifact.status_search_result: The general decidability of solvability of polynomial Diophantine equations is known to be undecidable (Hilbert's tenth problem, Matiyasevich 1970), and undecidability is known even with restricted numbers of variables. The specific homogeneous-with-all-nonzero-variables variant is posed as an open problem in a recent survey of open Diophantine problems and no resolution was located. Its status is best classified as open.

status_evidence.title: Hilbert's tenth problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Hilbert's tenth problem has been solved with a negative answer... Matiyasevich completing the theorem in 1970.
status_evidence.claim: The general decision problem for integer solutions of polynomial Diophantine equations is undecidable, motivating restricted variants such as the homogeneous all-nonzero version.

status_evidence.title: A systematic approach to Diophantine equations: open problems (arXiv:2404.08518)
status_evidence.snippet: polynomial Diophantine equations that are simple to state but apparently difficult to solve
status_evidence.claim: The homogeneous-equation question with all variables nonzero is listed among open problems in this collection.
